headline: Highest risk is data leakage from marker’s local document handling into opik’s broad-egress REST API path; other pairwise risks are limited by missing shared surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: marker has no filesystem write, browser, subprocess, or MCP surfaces, and opik exposes only a REST API with no documented ingestion bridge from marker. With no shared communication channel or parser path, prompt injection between them is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies marker output into opik prompts or API payloads, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared clipboard, queue, or filesystem bridge is added, reassess for prompt injection.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except through explicit, sanitized fields.
Strip instructions from marker outputs before any downstream use.
Use allowlisted JSON schemas for any marker-to-opik handoff.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: marker is a document-processing agent with no local write or network egress, while opik has broad network egress and REST API calls. If marker processes sensitive documents and its outputs or context are forwarded to opik, leakage can occur in default-style integrations even though no shared workspace is documented.
conditions: IF marker is given sensitive documents and opik receives their contents or summaries, leakage is possible.
IF an integration forwards marker context to opik over REST, data may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Minimize data sent from marker to opik.
Redact secrets before forwarding any text.
Disable or scope opik network destinations.
Use synthetic samples for evaluation runs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss prevention on the handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marker cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and opik is not runnable and only exposes REST API calls. There is no overlapping mutable resource or write surface in the profiles, so capability conflict is effectively blocked.
conditions: IF opik is wrapped in a separate writable orchestrator with shared state, conflict risk should be re-evaluated.
IF marker gains write or git permissions, overlapping writes may emerge.
mitigations: Keep marker read-only.
Avoid shared mutable workspaces.
Run opik in a separate process boundary.
Document any future shared-state orchestration.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: marker can generate document outputs that opik may consume through its REST API path, so A’s output can become B’s input. Because opik is an evaluation/observability tool, the main risk is unverified propagation of incorrect extracted facts rather than direct autonomous action, but the pathway exists in plausible integrations.
conditions: IF opik ingests marker outputs without validation, errors can cascade into downstream evaluations or reports.
IF marker output is treated as authoritative text, opik may preserve or amplify mistakes.
mitigations: Add a verification step before opik ingestion.
Require source citations for extracted claims.
Flag low-confidence marker outputs.
Sample-check a small batch before scaling.
requires-engineering: implement automated consistency checks between extraction and evaluation.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent, so a concrete compliance breach is not established. The only visible compliance-relevant difference is marker’s local document-processing posture versus opik’s broad egress, which could matter if regulated data is introduced, but that is not evidenced here.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by marker and forwarded to opik, compliance review is required.
IF either agent is later assigned residency or retention obligations, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pairing.
Check vendor terms before production use.
Log what data classes are sent to opik.
Use anonymized test corpora.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for regulated records.
